prerequisites: No specific prerequisites. Competencies from the modules Theoretical Computer Science, Logic, and Software Engineering are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to formalize systems, system properties, and software development activities.
Students can explain how system properties can be automatically analyzed and verified.
Students can assess the strengths and weaknesses of formal methods in software engineering.
Students are able to apply scientific working methods in independently identifying, formulating, and solving problems.
Students are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

syllabus_topics: Finite automata for formal specification of simple systems
Refinement of state specification using data structures for realistic systems
Graphs for flexible specification of data structures
Graph transformations for systematically defining changes in data structures
Formal specification and analysis of typical software development activities (e.g., system design, program testing)
Development of a specification and analysis technique for a selected software engineering problem

assessment_methods.method: Weekly exercise assignments (minimum 50% of points required)
Oral presentation of solutions to at least two exercise assignments

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, students must achieve at least 50% of the points from the weekly exercise assignments and orally present the solution to at least two of these assignments. The examination performance is either an oral examination (individual examination) or a written examination. Grading is done on a scale of 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science program.
